subject: science

entries: Light arrives as a stream of photons: photons rain onto the metal plate one packet at a time, each carrying energy h f fixed by the frequency, and one electron may absorb a whole packet in a single exchange.
slots.label: Light arrives as a stream of photons
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Below the threshold frequency, nothing happens: the photons each carry less than the work function, so however many arrive the surface stays silent - only past the threshold do electrons start to fly.
slots.label: Below the threshold frequency, nothing happens
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Einstein's photoelectric equation: the photon energy h f first pays the work function W to free the electron, and whatever remains becomes the electron's kinetic energy, h f = W + KE_max.
slots.label: Einstein's photoelectric equation
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Brighter light: more photons, more electrons: doubling the intensity doubles the photons arriving per second, so twice as many electrons escape, each with exactly the same speed as before - same-length arrows, twice as many.
slots.label: Brighter light
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Misconception: brighter light ejects faster electrons: the brighter beam only raises the electron count, and the dim violet beam still ejects faster electrons than the bright red one, because speed comes from frequency alone.
slots.label: Misconception
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A single packet of light energy, carrying E = h f where f is the light’s frequency: one photon is absorbed whole by one electron in the photoelectric effect.
slots.label: Photon
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The minimum energy W an electron needs to escape a metal surface, a property of the metal: the photon must pay at least W before any kinetic energy is left over.
slots.label: Work function
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The lowest frequency f0 = W / h whose photons can free an electron: below f0 no emission occurs at any intensity, at f0 the emitted electrons have zero kinetic energy.
slots.label: Threshold frequency
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The retarding potential V_s that just stops even the fastest emitted electrons, e V_s = KE_max: it measures the maximum kinetic energy and depends on frequency, not intensity.
slots.label: Stopping potential
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The emission of electrons when light above the threshold frequency strikes a metal, one photon freeing one electron: its frequency threshold and instant emission are evidence that light arrives as photons.
slots.label: Photoelectric effect
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The two-sided nature of light and matter: light travels as waves but exchanges energy as photons, and moving particles carry a de Broglie wavelength λ = h / (m v).
slots.label: Wave-particle duality
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: JC H2 physics — quantum: photons and the photoelectric effect
